verdict.rationale: AssemblyAI lets users steer transcription output with natural-language instructions: formatting instructions sent with the audio return a cleaned-up transcript, and contextual prompting is supported. Its LLM Gateway also applies language models to transcripts, for example to generate meeting notes. This is natural-language direction of specific processing steps, not general operation of the product by natural-language command; the Docs MCP server only serves documentation lookups and is not credited. missing for 10: natural-language control of the product's operations beyond transcript formatting and prompting (e.g., submitting jobs or configuring features by command), an agent-operable control interface, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: You include formatting instructions with your audio, and the transcript comes back already cleaned up and formatted.
Gives unified access to frontier language models through the same API, so teams can apply reasoning models to their transcription without a separate integration.
